learningObjective: Distinguish ReduceScatter from AllReduce and identify how the two compose.
stem: Given N ranks each holding a tensor of shape S, which statement about ReduceScatter is correct?

options.text: ReduceScatter reduces the N tensors elementwise and delivers the full reduced tensor of shape S to rank 0 only; other ranks receive nothing.
ReduceScatter is a naming alias for All-to-All when the payload contains only one element per rank; the two are semantically identical for scalar payloads.
ReduceScatter is equivalent to AllGather followed by a local reduction on each rank, so it always ends with every rank holding the full reduced tensor of shape S.
ReduceScatter reduces the N tensors elementwise and gives each rank a disjoint 1/N-shard of the result, so AllReduce = ReduceScatter followed by AllGather.

explanation: ReduceScatter is a hybrid primitive: it applies an associative reduction across ranks and then distributes disjoint shards of the reduced tensor to each rank. Because AllGather concatenates those shards on every rank, AllReduce is semantically ReduceScatter ∘ AllGather. Ring-AllReduce is often implemented exactly this way.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: that describes Reduce (single-recipient), not ReduceScatter.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: All-to-All permutes payloads without any reduction; the two have distinct semantics.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: no rank ends with the full reduced tensor after ReduceScatter alone.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: reduces then distributes 1/N-shards, and ReduceScatter ∘ AllGather = AllReduce.

assumptions: All ranks contribute tensors of identical shape and dtype.
The scatter axis divides the tensor evenly into N shards.
nonImplications: Does not imply that ReduceScatter and AllReduce cost the same; ReduceScatter's ring-cost is (N-1)/N · S per rank, half of AllReduce.
Does not imply that ReduceScatter is exclusive to FSDP; it is the first half of ring-AllReduce.
